families.name: Metric Paint
families.summary: Conditionally rewrite cells selected by distance from an event center.
families.rule: PAINT(a,r,u,v): simultaneously replace u by v at every coordinate x with sum_i |x_i-a_i| <= r. All other cells remain unchanged.

example.card: On shape [7], listing the values of cells [0] to [6] in order. Before: 1 2 0 1 3 1 0. Event: {"op":"PAINT","a":[3],"r":2,"u":1,"v":3}. After: 1 2 0 3 3 3 0. The ball is cells [1] to [5]. Among them, [3] and [5] hold 1 and become 3; the 2 at [1] and the 3 at [4] are unchanged. Cell [0] also holds 1 but lies outside the ball and is unchanged.

families.name: Box Reflection
families.summary: Reflect the contents of an axis-aligned box along one coordinate axis.
families.rule: REFLECT(lo,hi,axis): for every cell x in the inclusive box lo <= x <= hi, the new value at the mirrored position x' (x'_axis = lo_axis + hi_axis - x_axis, other coordinates unchanged) is the old value at x, including 0. All writes happen simultaneously. Cells outside the box remain unchanged.

example.card: On shape [6], listing the values of cells [0] to [5] in order. Before: 1 2 3 0 0 1. Event: {"op":"REFLECT","axis":0,"hi":[4],"lo":[1]}. After: 1 0 0 3 2 1. The box is cells [1] to [4]; their old values 2 3 0 0 are written back in reverse order as 0 0 3 2, so the zeros move as well. Cells [0] and [5] are outside the box and keep their values.

families.name: Local Stencil
families.summary: Synchronously propagate integer state through local neighbourhoods in a ball.
families.structure: Axis neighbourhoods of every cell in a Manhattan ball
families.rule: STENCIL(a,r): simultaneously set every cell x with sum_i |x_i-a_i| <= r to (W(x) + sum W(y)) mod 4, where y ranges over the in-bounds cells at Manhattan distance 1 from x, whether or not they lie within distance r of a. Every update reads the same old world; cells farther than r from a remain unchanged.

example.card: On shape [7], listing the values of cells [0] to [6] in order. Before: 1 2 0 1 3 0 2. Event: {"op":"STENCIL","a":[3],"r":1}. After: 1 2 3 0 0 0 2. Only cells [2], [3], and [4] lie within distance 1 of [3]. Cell [2] becomes (0+2+1) mod 4 = 3 from its own value and its neighbours [1] and [3]; cell [3] becomes (1+0+3) mod 4 = 0; cell [4] becomes (3+1+0) mod 4 = 0. Cells [1] and [5] are read as neighbours but are not changed.

families.name: Occluded Mix
families.summary: Modular aggregation over the region reachable from p through nonzero cells.
families.structure: Axis neighbourhoods of every cell within r steps of p through nonzero cells
families.rule: MIX(p,r): if W(p) = 0, nothing changes. Otherwise find every cell that can be reached from p by a path of at most r Manhattan-distance-1 steps whose cells all have nonzero old values (p itself counts as reached with 0 steps; a cell with old value 0 can never be entered or passed through). Then simultaneously set every reached cell x to 1 + ((W(x) + sum W(y)) mod 3), where y ranges over the in-bounds cells at Manhattan distance 1 from x, whether or not they were reached. Every update reads the old world; cells that were not reached remain unchanged.

example.card: On shape [7], listing the values of cells [0] to [6] in order. Before: 2 1 1 3 0 1 2. Event: {"op":"MIX","p":[2],"r":2}. After: 1 2 3 2 0 1 2. From [2], cells [1] and [3] are reached in one step and [0] in two steps. Cell [4] is 0 and cannot be entered, so [5] and [6] are never reached although [5] is within distance 3 of [2]. Cell [0] becomes 1 + ((2+1) mod 3) = 1 from its own value and its neighbour [1]; cell [1] becomes 1 + ((1+2+1) mod 3) = 2; cell [2] becomes 1 + ((1+1+3) mod 3) = 3; cell [3] becomes 1 + ((3+1+0) mod 3) = 2, reading the 0 at [4] although [4] is not reached. A reached cell is never set to 0.

families.name: Component Relabel
families.summary: Relabel a maximal equal-valued component under axis adjacency.
families.rule: RELABEL(p,v): let u = W(p) (u may be 0). Find the maximal set of cells connected to p by Manhattan-distance-1 steps whose old values are all u, including p. Set every cell of that set to v.

example.card: On shape [7], listing the values of cells [0] to [6] in order. Before: 1 1 0 1 2 2 3. Event: {"op":"RELABEL","p":[4],"v":3}. After: 1 1 0 1 3 3 3. The cells with old value 2 connected to [4] are [4] and [5]; both become 3. The 1 at [3] and the 3 at [6] are not part of that set, although [6] ends up adjacent to the new 3s.

families.name: Boundary Layer
families.summary: Strip the exposed layer of a component, or grow it into its empty neighbours.
families.rule: LAYER(p,s): if W(p) = 0, nothing changes. Otherwise let u = W(p) and find the maximal Manhattan-connected set of cells with old value u, including p. If s = -1, set to 0 every cell of that set that has an in-bounds neighbor with old value 0. If s = +1, set to u every in-bounds cell with old value 0 that is a neighbor of a cell of that set. Positions outside the world are not neighbors; nothing else changes.

example.card: On shape [7], listing the values of cells [0] to [6] in order. Before: 0 1 1 1 2 0 1. Event: {"op":"LAYER","p":[2],"s":-1}. After: 0 0 1 1 2 0 1. The cells with value 1 connected to [2] are [1], [2], and [3]. Cell [1] has the neighbor [0] with value 0, so it becomes 0; [2] and [3] have no neighbor with value 0 and keep their value. With s = +1 the event {"op":"LAYER","p":[2],"s":1} would instead set [0] to 1. The 1 at [6] is a different set and is never touched.

families.name: Obstructed Motion
families.summary: Move selected entities along an axis subject to boundaries and obstruction.
families.rule: MOVE(v,axis,direction,k): take every cell with value v, ordered by decreasing coordinate on axis if direction=1 and increasing if direction=-1, so that the cells nearest the leading edge are handled first. In that order, move each one along axis in the sign of direction, one cell at a time and at most k cells, stopping as soon as the next cell is outside the world or nonzero (including cells already moved into). Each move clears the old cell and writes v to the new cell; values never merge, and a block of adjacent v cells therefore moves as a unit.

example.card: On shape [7], listing the values of cells [0] to [6] in order. Before: 1 1 0 0 2 0 1. Event: {"op":"MOVE","axis":0,"direction":1,"k":2,"v":1}. After: 0 0 1 1 2 0 1. The cells holding 1 are handled from the highest coordinate down. [6] cannot move because the next cell is outside the world; [1] moves to [3]; then [0] moves to [2] through the cell that [1] vacated. The 2 at [4] is never moved.

families.name: Aggregating Compression
families.summary: Globally compact axis-aligned fibers and merge equal adjacent values.
families.rule: COMPRESS(axis,direction): on every line parallel to axis, independently: list the nonzero values in order starting from the destination edge (coordinate 0 if direction=-1, the highest coordinate if direction=1). Walk that list from its start; whenever two consecutive values are equal, replace them by one value equal to their sum and continue after the pair, so a merged value cannot merge again in this event. Write the resulting list back starting at the destination edge and set every remaining cell of the line to 0.

example.card: On shape [6], listing the values of cells [0] to [5] in order. Before: 1 1 2 0 1 0. Event: {"op":"COMPRESS","axis":0,"direction":-1}. After: 2 2 1 0 0 0. The nonzero values read from the destination edge are 1 1 2 1. The first pair merges into 2; that merged 2 is not merged again with the 2 that follows it; the final 1 is kept. The result 2 2 1 is written from cell [0] and the remaining cells become 0.
